title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 21
paragraphs: When the Milesians suffered this treatment from the Persians, the men of Sybaris, who were living in Laüs and Scidrus after being deprived of their own city, did not repay like with like. For when Sybaris was taken by the men of Croton, the Milesians all from youth upwards shaved their heads and put on great mourning; for these cities were bound together by ties of friendship more than any other cities we know of. The Athenians, by contrast, were unlike the Sybarites; they made it clear that they were grieved at the capture of Miletus in many ways, and especially in this: that when Phrynichus had composed a drama called “The Capture of Miletus” and put it on stage, the body of spectators fell to weeping, and the Athenians moreover fined the poet a thousand drachmas on the ground that he had reminded them of their own calamities; and they ordered also that no one in future should produce this drama.
